<thought>The 13C NMR spectrum shows two low‑field carbon signals at 26.29 ppm and 43.30 ppm. Carbons in the 10–30 ppm range are typical for methyl (CH₃) groups; a signal at ~43 ppm is more consistent with a methylene or a carbon attached to an electronegative atom rather than a methyl. Therefore, only one carbon signal corresponds to a methyl group. The molecule thus contains a single CH₃ group.</thought>
<final_answer>1</final_answer>
